The site is VeloFix Mobile Mechanic — Doorstep Bicycle Tuning & Repair, a booking web application for Mobile bicycle mechanic service booking.

Owner brief: "I operate a mobile bicycle repair van visiting customers at their homes or offices. I need a straightforward booking application where cyclists select a tune-up package, enter their location and preferred time slot, and receive a confirmed appointment reference. The booking must be stored on the server so reloading the confirmation route preserves their booking details, and all form controls must announce validation errors clearly."

Locale & copy conventions (en-GB): Use £ prices, British English spelling, day-month dates and .co.uk-style invented domains. Today's date is 11 October 2026; date all entries, bookings, deadlines, and activity in the weeks after 11 October 2026.

Visual identity & layout lock: Match the exact brand header, logo treatment, navigation bar, typography, card geometry, and light colour palette of the attached reference image (docs/design/training/tr-01/reference.jpg).

Art direction: VeloFix Mobile Mechanic — Doorstep Bicycle Tuning & Repair: the page for mobile bicycle mechanic service booking, in a dark, low-glare palette, recognisable by its own token prefix rather than by a shared template.

Use this exact Light Mode colour palette: #0f172a (vf-bg), #1e293b (vf-surface), #273549 (vf-card), #334155 (vf-border), #10b981 (vf-accent), #059669 (vf-accent-hover), #f8fafc (vf-text), #94a3b8 (vf-text-muted). The primary accent colour carries the single primary action.

Structural constants: control-radius 8px, content-frame 1200px, control-border 1px solid var(--vf-border), page-padding 1.5rem. Keep every form control clearly identifiable in its unfocused state with a distinct background fill or icon cue.

Strictly avoid: a calendar widget that hides the available slots behind extra clicks; a second accent colour competing with the primary action; placeholder text standing in for a visible label; a modal or step wizard hiding part of the form; colour alone carrying an error with no message naming the field.

STEP 1 OF 4 (LIGHT MODE) — INITIAL OVERVIEW & READY WORKSPACE:

Render the initial landing state of VeloFix Mobile Mechanic — Doorstep Bicycle Tuning & Repair as a visitor first meets it on the primary workspace. Top-to-bottom structure: a brand header, then a navigation bar, then a main content area, then a content section, then the working form, then a group of fields (3 of them), then a footer.

Show the active overview/dashboard/ledger/catalogue surface populated with realistic, internally consistent records and totals, alongside the ready-to-use interactive form with visible labels for every control ("Full name", "Contact phone", "Service address", "Tune-up package", "Preferred time slot", "Access notes").

User journey context: Browse available tune-up packages, choose a service, and proceed to booking. Enter contact details, service address, and select a time slot to submit. View the booking confirmation reference and reload the page to confirm persistence.

Include editorial photography where appropriate to the subject, a concise social-proof or status summary row, and the complete site footer.
